A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UFO, retaining the central formulation and many experiments. The text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial additions and reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original multi-task, visual grounding and ReasonSeg experiments, ablations, and appendix evaluations on retinal vessel segmentation and depth estimation.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and reports additional VQA evaluations, full-data retinal vessel segmentation and surface-normal prediction results.

M1.justification: The core box representation, mask retrieval, upsampling and losses remain unchanged. Appendix G adds a surface-normal adaptation using three directional tokens and normalization of their predicted components. Expanded descriptions of parallel decoding and post-processing do not establish changes to those existing procedures.

E1.justification: v3 adds GQA, MMBench, MMVP and HallusionBench evaluations and NYUv2 surface-normal prediction; depth estimation and DRIVE were already present. Instruction-tuning coverage adds LLaVA-OneVision VQA data for InternVL2.5 and removes PACO-LVIS/PASCAL-Part part-segmentation sources and OpenImages detection data, while retaining OpenImages instance segmentation (v1 Table 9; v3 Table 8).

E2.justification: The grounding comparison removes LISA, PixelLM and NExT-Chat, adds GLaMM and HiMTok, and replaces Ferret and SAM4MLLM configurations (v1 Table 4; v3 Table 3). ReasonSeg adds Cores and HiMTok while removing GRES and the LISA-LLaVA-1.5 rows. Table 2 drops Pix2Seq, and new DRIVE and surface-normal comparisons introduce additional specialists.

E3.justification: Reported instruction-tuning settings change substantially: InternVL2 becomes InternVL2.5; equal task/dataset sampling becomes unequal task weights and dataset-size-based sampling; default-resolution training becomes 90k low-resolution plus 30k high-resolution iterations. Dataset amounts are revised, including REC/RES from 0.8M to 85K. Full-training-set DRIVE evaluation and surface-normal angular metrics add protocols. These disclosures establish reported setting changes, without establishing which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v1 Table 17's task-data contribution ablation is removed. v3 adds paired base-versus-UFO VQA preservation tests and a trainable-parameter efficiency comparison, extends the loss-weight ablation with a 1:5 setting, and replaces two failure cases. Most core ViT ablations remain; the advanced-training-strategy study moves to Appendix F rather than being newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental error bars, confidence intervals, significance tests, seeds or repeated-run counts. v3's checklist explicitly acknowledges the absence of statistical-significance reporting because of computational cost, but introduces no uncertainty estimates or statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Grounding and ReasonSeg results are extensively updated: UFO-LLaVA's unfine-tuned RES average changes from 72.4 to 75.2, while fine-tuned InternVL ReasonSeg changes from 61.2 for InternVL2 to 67.0 for InternVL2.5. Changed training/model settings prevent interpreting these as same-setting gains. v3 also adds VQA, full-data DRIVE and surface-normal results, updates depth and qualitative results, and removes the data-contribution results. Table 2's ViT scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix G adds mathematical definitions for three surface-normal components and their normalization into a unit vector. Existing segmentation and depth equations are retained. The expanded decoding equations express the existing procedure; neither version contains theorem-and-proof results.

C1.justification: v3 removes the introduction's claim to be the first such framework and changes the third contribution from broadly competitive fine-grained perception to outperforming previous state-of-the-art ReasonSeg methods, explicitly claiming a 6.2 gIoU advantage. The central unification claim and abstract's headline ViT improvements remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 interprets performance without explicit chain-of-thought as evidence of reasoning during mask-embedding generation and tentatively links HallusionBench performance to reduced hallucination. Failure explanations change from counting and occluded-region ambiguity to low visibility and overlapping similar objects. Interpretations of individual training-data contributions disappear with their ablation; the main task-synergy explanation remains.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents text parsing, first-token confidence scoring and NMS, and clarifies trainable text embeddings and LoRA parameter counts. It also specifies dataset subsampling and revised training schedules. Conversely, the explicit 239-sample ReasonSeg fine-tuning disclosure is removed, without establishing a changed sample count. Most existing implementation details and the code/model link are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion of HiMTok's specialized decoder and Text4Seg's refiner, connects parallel decoding to blockwise prediction, and incorporates newer MLLM, VQA and geometry references. The first-framework novelty wording is removed. These update the positioning while retaining the central comparison against task decoders, polygon representations and GiT.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much of the prose remain intact. Selected introduction and results passages are rewritten, open-ended and parallel-decoding explanations are expanded, and the advanced-training ablation moves to the appendix. The supplement receives alphabetical headings, and a conference checklist and broader-impacts section are added.

P2.justification: The paper changes throughout from two-column formatting to a single-column NeurIPS layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of tables and figures. Figure 3 separates box and mask templates, retinal visualizations are consolidated, and qualitative examples change. New VQA, parameter-count, DRIVE and surface-normal tables accompany removal of the earlier dataset-summary and task-data-ablation displays.

improvement.justification: v3 improves assessment of retained VQA capabilities, updates competitive comparisons and clarifies implementation while preserving the main ViT evidence. These gains are tempered by removal of v1's task-data ablation and reporting problems in the new surface-normal evidence, including the anomalous 9.502 entry in Table 21. The net improvement is limited; higher MLLM scores under changed settings do not independently establish better methodology.
